title: Word order 1
subtitle: The verb in second place, questions, and time before place

explain.text: In a Dutch statement the conjugated verb is always the **second element**. The first element is often the subject, but it can also be a time, a place or something else you want to stress. When it is not the subject, the subject moves behind the verb. This is called **inversion**.
The first *element* can be several words: *Op zaterdag* or *In de zomer* count as one block. Then comes the verb. Never put the subject between the first block and the verb: *Morgen ik ga* is wrong.

explain.nl: Op zaterdag eten wij bij mijn oma.
explain.en: On Saturday we eat at my grandma's.

items.q: Which word must be second in the sentence?

items.en: Today I work at home.

items.text: Op zaterdag ___ wij naar de markt.
items.en: On Saturday we go to the market.

explain.text: A **yes/no question** starts with the verb: *Woon je in Utrecht?* A **question word** goes first, then the verb, then the subject: *Waar woon je?* Remember the verb is always in second place.

explain.en: What time does the lesson start?

explain.text: Use **welk** with *het*-words and **welke** with *de*-words and plurals: *welk boek, welke tafel, welke boeken*. Use **hoe laat** to ask for the time: *Hoe laat is het?*

items.explain: boek is a het-word, so welk.
fiets is a de-word, so welke.

Where are you from? From Spain.

items.text: ___ laat is het? Het is half drie.
items.en: What time is it? It is half past two.

items.text: ___ vertrekt de trein? Om tien uur.

explain.text: After the verb, extra information usually follows a fixed order: **time** first, then **manner** (how or with whom), then **place**. Think *TMP*: Time – Manner – Place.

explain.nl: Ik ga morgen met de bus naar Utrecht.
explain.en: I am going to Utrecht by bus tomorrow.

explain.text: If you swap the order, people will still understand you, but time before place sounds more natural. Most of the time you only need two of the three parts.

items.q: Which sentence has the natural order?
options: Ik ga met de bus morgen naar Utrecht.
Ik ga morgen met de bus naar Utrecht.
Ik ga naar Utrecht morgen met de bus.

items.q: Which sentence has the natural order?
options: Hij werkt in de tuin elke dag.
Hij werkt elke dag in de tuin.
Hij elke dag werkt in de tuin.
